# Social Engineering Experts (Crypto challenge)

I found this Cryptography challenge on [CTFtime](https://ctftime.org/team/151372). It looked like `Social Engineering Experts` was recruiting new members.&#x20;

It reads `Join us - but first, solve a challenge: https://forms.gle/o4mYdmpT6KTRc31M9`

![](<../.gitbook/assets/image (530).png>)

I have been looking for a team to participate in CTF competitions since 2020 so this was a great opportunity. Furthermore, I wanted to challenge myself to see if I could solve their challenge!

I found this challenge on 28 June 2022 and it was solved on the same day.

On the Google forms, we can choose between Cryptography or Reverse Engineering challenge.

Since we only need to solve one of the challenges, I choose the Cryptography challenge.

Despite getting the correct flag for this challenge and writing a short introduction about myself and my interest in cybersecurity, I have not heard back from `Social Engineering Experts` after weeks.

Update: After slightly more than a month, on the 8 August 2022, founder of `Social Engineering Experts` CTF team, Zeyu replied.

![](<../.gitbook/assets/image (798).png>)

I have officially joined the `Social Engineering Experts` CTF Team on 8 August 2022 :)

## Cryptography

![](<../.gitbook/assets/image (513).png>)

![](<../.gitbook/assets/image (519).png>)

For this challenge we were given some parameters and the goal is to find out what was sent to `Agent Rainbow` and `Agent Pigeon`. Here are the parameters provided in the challenge:

```
n = 
e1 = 65503
e2 = 65531
c1 = 
c2 = 
```

This was kind of a new concept to me. I had solved cryptography challenges before like `RSA` or simple decryption type of challenges but I have not solved anything similar to this before.

At first glance, this challenge might seem a little daunting, with 5 different large values for `n`,`e1`,`e2`,`c1` and `c2`. However, after some searching online, I found this pretty good [website](https://blog.katastros.com/a?ID=01800-975cfd2e-2e97-41d7-9a34-38192a61da77) which presented `Common question types about RSA in CTF`.

I scroll down till number 5 and realised it looked similar to the challenge here.

![](<../.gitbook/assets/image (542).png>)

Next, I opened up [Sublime Text](https://www.sublimetext.com/) to edit the Python script.

![](<../.gitbook/assets/image (524).png>)

The python script can be found below

```python
import gmpy2
import binascii

n = 
c1 = 
c2 = 
e1 =  65503
e2 =  65531

s = gmpy2 . gcdext ( e1 , e2 ) 
a = s [ 1 ] 
b = s [ 2 ]

if a < 0 : 
    a =  - a
    c1 = gmpy2 . invert ( c1 , n ) 
else : 
    b =  - b
    c2 = gmpy2 . invert ( c2 , n )

m =  ( gmpy2 . powmod ( c1 , a , n ) * gmpy2 . powmod ( c2 , b , n ) ) % n

print ( binascii . unhexlify ( hex ( m ) [ 2 : ] ) )
```

Running the script would give me the flag
